specification_compliance: I8 (r7 CR7-1): fixed. PageImages now acquires PYMUPDF_LOCK once in open() (at most 30 s) and holds it until close(), which _serve_page_request calls in its outer finally (rag.py:2351-2352). A render failure raised from _render_page is caught inside the loop (rag.py:2347-2350). The traceback, and with it the Page and Pixmap, is freed when `exc` is unbound at the end of that except clause, while the lock is still held. On success the Page and Pixmap are freed when _render_page returns, also under the lock.

I8 (r7 CR7-2): fixed. close() calls document.close() and sets self._document = None before the lock is released in its finally. Nothing else holds the Document, so it is deallocated under the lock. The daemon-thread close and _close_locked are gone.

I8, open failure: if pymupdf.open raises after the lock was taken, _held is True, so close() still releases the lock. The exception is unbound inside page_count()'s except clause, while the lock is held. If acquire times out, PageImageUnavailable(lock_timeout) is raised, _held stays False, and close() does nothing.

I7: each page that passed the rules and hits a lock timeout or open failure is named `not available` and takes no number (rag.py:2342-2344). The 30 s wait is per page request, which matches spec §1.9.3.
I1-I6 and I9: rag.py has no product change in this round. My earlier reading stands.
r6 B findings CR-3 and CR-4, and r7 B unspecified items about the title cut, were not touched in this round.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: A page request now holds PYMUPDF_LOCK for its whole run, from the first page-count need through rendering up to 4 pages, instead of taking it once per PyMuPDF call.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: An extraction or OCR that starts while a page request runs waits a few seconds more for the lock. The user sees nothing.

regression_risks: An extraction now waits behind the whole page request, up to 4 renders, rather than behind single calls. That is bounded by 4 renders of 1280 px each.

In the hygiene test, weakref.finalize on pymupdf.Page assumes that Page supports weak references in the installed PyMuPDF. If it does not, the test's own _render raises TypeError and the test fails, not the product.
test_coverage: test_every_pymupdf_object_is_freed_under_the_lock_even_when_a_page_fails covers the Page freed on the render-failure path, the Page and Pixmap freed on success, and Document.close, all checked with the lock held. Moving the render outside the lock, or closing the page source before the except clause, would fail it.
Document deallocation, as opposed to the close call, is not checked (CR8-2).
The 30 s lock-timeout test still holds the lock before open(), and it now matches the single acquire in open().

trajectory: The record has three rounds. The r6→r7 fix added state and branches to PageImages: a shared monotonic budget, a `_locked` context manager taken per call, an explicit `del pixmap, page`, and in close() a timed acquire plus a daemon-thread fallback through `_close_locked`. The r8 fix (54f131c) adds no branch, state or prediction that r7 also added. It removes all of them: `_close_locked`, the daemon thread, the `_locked` context manager, the `_end` budget and the explicit `del`. In their place is one structure: one acquire in open(), held until close() in the caller's finally, with render failures handled inside that hold. This round simplifies the design rather than patching it. Its only leftovers are three unused imports (CR8-1) and an untested deallocation (CR8-2).
